pull.title: MINOR: Use Locale.ROOT for the SCRAM iteration count and remove the unused credential string format
pull.body:
`ScramMessages.ServerFirstMessage.toMessage()` builds the SCRAM
server-first-message with `String.format("r=%s,s=%s,i=%d", ...)`.
Without an explicit `Locale`, `%d` follows the JVM's default locale, and
on a broker whose default locale uses native digits (for example
`ar-EG`, `fa-IR`, `bn-BD`, `ne-NP`; JDK 9+ CLDR data) the iteration
count is emitted as `i=٤٠٩٦` instead of `i=4096`.

RFC 5802 requires ASCII digits, and `ServerFirstMessage` itself parses
the count with `i=(?<iterations>[0-9]+)`, so every SCRAM handshake
against such a broker fails with `SaslException: Invalid SCRAM server
first message format: r=...,i=٤٠٩٦` (non-Java clients reject it the same
way).

This passes `Locale.ROOT` to that `String.format` call, as already done
for `toLowerCase()` under KAFKA-20638 and for the
`tools`/`server-common` modules under KAFKA-20646 (which does not cover
`clients`), and adds a test that switches the default locale to `ar-EG`
(guarded with `@ResourceLock(Resources.LOCALE)`) and verifies the
message still uses ASCII digits. The other `String.format` calls in
`ScramMessages` only use `%s` and are not locale-sensitive.

Following review, it also removes
`ScramCredentialUtils.credentialToString()` / `credentialFromString()`:
the ZooKeeper-era credential string format had the same `%d` problem but
no callers left outside its own tests, so the methods, their constants
and the tests that only exercised them are gone.
`ScramCredentialUtils.createCache()` and its test are unchanged.

Reproduced against the released `kafka-clients` 4.4.0 jar on JDK 25:
```
java -Duser.language=ar -Duser.country=EG ...
server-first-message on the wire =
r=clientnonceservernonce,s=MDEy...,i=٤٠٩٦
client parse                     = FAILED: Invalid SCRAM server first
message format
```

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reviewers: Andrew Schofield <aschofield@confluent.io>

reviews.body: Thanks for the PR. It seems to me that some of this code is changing legacy code from ZooKeeper days which could probably just be removed.
Thanks for the updates. Looks good to me.

review_comments.body: This appears to be code that is no longer used, apart from a handful of tests.
This is a JVM-wide global state which is being changed. Consider `@ResourceLock(Resources.LOCALE)` to ensure that concurrent execution of other tests will not fall foul of the local change.

Agreed. `credentialToString`/`credentialFromString` (the ZooKeeper credential-store format) have no callers left outside `ScramCredentialUtilsTest`, so I removed them together with `toProps`, the field-name constants and the tests that only exercised them. `createCache` stays (still used by `CredentialProvider` and `DelegationTokenCache`), and so does its `scramCredentialCache` test. The `Locale.ROOT` fix is now only in `ServerFirstMessage.toMessage()`.
Done, `serverFirstMessageUsesAsciiDigitsRegardlessOfDefaultLocale` now carries `@ResourceLock(Resources.LOCALE)`. The other locale test went away with the removed credential string format.

commit.message:
MINOR: Use Locale.ROOT when formatting SCRAM iteration counts

ServerFirstMessage.toMessage() and ScramCredentialUtils.credentialToString()
format the iteration count with String.format("%d") and no explicit Locale,
so on a JVM whose default locale uses native digits (for example ar-EG or
fa-IR) the server-first-message is sent as "i=٤٠٩٦" instead of "i=4096".
RFC 5802 requires ASCII digits and ServerFirstMessage parses the count with
[0-9]+, so every SCRAM handshake against such a broker fails with
"Invalid SCRAM server first message format". The persisted credential
string has the same problem.

Pass Locale.ROOT to both calls and add tests that switch the default
locale to ar-EG and verify the message and the credential string still
use ASCII digits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

MINOR: Guard the SCRAM locale test with @ResourceLock(Resources.LOCALE)

serverFirstMessageUsesAsciiDigitsRegardlessOfDefaultLocale switches the
JVM-wide default locale, so declare the LOCALE resource lock to keep it
from interfering with other tests under concurrent execution.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

MINOR: Remove the unused ZooKeeper-era SCRAM credential string format

ScramCredentialUtils.credentialToString() and credentialFromString()
implemented the credential-store format used when SCRAM credentials were
persisted in ZooKeeper. Nothing calls them any more apart from their own
tests, so remove them together with toProps(), the field-name constants
and those tests. createCache() and its test are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
